facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old male
past medical history of hypertension and coronary artery disease
episodes of prominent dizziness, vertigo, intermittent left arm shaking, and bouts of dull response
each episode lasted about 5 minutes
the attacks recurred more than 10 times a day
no prior history of seizures
Blood pressure was 200/110 mmHg at triage
neurological examination was unremarkable except for the presence of a dull response during the events
no focal brainstem signs, left-right disorientation, dyslexia, dysgraphia, or finger agnosia
Brain MRI revealed non-specific white matter changes
rhythmic epileptiform discharges originating from the right frontal area
activities appeared in a quasi-periodic fashion at intervals of about one second
